A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAB/TAB4IDC research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching the retained appendix galleries across renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original captioning, localization, attention-intervention, ablation, and zero-shot experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and adds experiments on attention-supervised CLIP4IDC intervention in Section 5.3 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The proposed one-head co-attention bottleneck, removed skip connection, dynamic attention gating, and two-stage training objectives remain unchanged. Training an attention-supervised CLIP4IDC control does not change TAB itself.

E1.justification: Both versions cover CLEVR-Change, OpenImages-I, and Spot-the-Diff, with COCO-Inpainted already appearing as CYWS's training dataset. Added comparisons use the existing captioning and intervention tasks; no new evaluated domain or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 5 substantially broadens the Spot-the-Diff comparison by adding reported results for LLaVA-1.5-13B, Mini-Gemini-7B, InternVL2-8B, and OneDiff. Appendix D additionally compares TAB interventions against attention-supervised CLIP4IDC, which was absent from v1's intervention comparison.

E3.justification: V4 adds a control that trains CLIP4IDC with the same attention-supervision loss as TAB and applies the existing ZEROATTENTION and CORRECTATTENTION procedures. Previously reported TAB training budgets, preprocessing, metrics, and localization-threshold selection remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests whether attention supervision alone makes ordinary MHSA editable, providing a focused architectural control. The earlier attention-supervision ablation, resolution comparisons, zero-shot analysis, and extensive qualitative appendix examples remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Shared numerical results remain unchanged, but v4 adds substantial comparative findings. Table 5 reports, for example, OneDiff CIDEr 56.6 and Mini-Gemini 53.3 alongside TAB4IDC-B/16's retained 51.3; these are additional model comparisons, not version-to-version gains. Table 13 newly shows unchanged MHSA change/no-change accuracies under intervention, with object accuracy shifting only from 89.78 to 89.76 or 89.80.

T1.justification: The architectural and loss equations, including Equations 1–11, and the PG+ definition retain their mathematical substance. V4 adds no theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or revised formal assumption.

C1.justification: The main TAB contributions and performance claims remain. V4's introduction explicitly adds the finding that modifying ordinary ViT attention can leave outputs unchanged, sharpening the comparison with conventional attention. TAB's own causal-intervention claim was already present in v1.

C2.justification: V4 interprets the new MHSA control as evidence that architectural information leakage limits intervention and that supervision alone is insufficient. It also discusses OneDiff's larger models and training diversity, and adds an applicability qualification concerning VLMs lacking auxiliary CLS/REG tokens. Earlier limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly identifies the contrastive temperature as learnable, and Appendix D specifies supervision of CLIP4IDC's 12 attention heads. These are limited documentation additions; Appendix A's training recipes, visualization code, caption templates, and code/data links are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds references concerning registers, explanation debugging, modern image-difference models, VLM visual shortcomings, and real-world recognition failures. It also explicitly distinguishes attention-based debugging from factual model editing. The existing related-work framework and primary novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: V4 rewrites the opening motivation, revises intervention discussion and conclusion passages, simplifies training-stage subheadings, and inserts Appendix D. Most methodological exposition and the overall section sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: The main visual presentation is substantially reorganized: Figure 1 becomes a direct MHSA-versus-TAB intervention comparison, Table 5 expands, and Table 13 is added. V1 Figure 3 moves to Appendix B as Figure 8, other main-text illustrations are rearranged or replaced, and a Spot-the-Diff illustration is added. The extensive appendix galleries are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 strengthens the existing intervention argument with an attention-supervised MHSA control and provides broader captioning comparisons, including acknowledging OneDiff's stronger reported results. These improve evidential context without changing TAB's underlying results. Some interpretation remains overstated: 'no effects' is stronger than Table 13's small object-accuracy changes support. The net quality gain is useful but limited.
